headline: Every team in the league has now mismanaged its bench two weeks running, with Screaming Eagles sitting a 38.85-point Drake Maye in the week's costliest example
meme_brief: A guy benches his quarterback, that quarterback throws for a monster day anyway on the sideline, and the team still wins by 20 points — the fantasy equivalent of surviving a crash you caused yourself.
recap:
Joe Mama Angie Daddy continued to separate itself atop the league, beating demon44 143.9 to 96.65, the week's largest margin at 47.25 points, behind Brock Purdy (29.8) and Javonte Williams (31.8) even with Joe Burrow scoring 34 points from the bench. Dak to the Future handled Broke Dak Mountain 121.75 to 101.65 on the strength of CeeDee Lamb's 33.8, and Pukachu Chews You outlasted Chuba Bucky Doo 149.25 to 124.45 behind Bijan Robinson's 31.2 and Emanuel Wilson's 27.5.

The closest game of the week was Silverbacks' 2.5-point win over mikelanta, 123.2 to 120.7 — Kyle Monangai (29.5) and Nico Collins (29.3) got it done despite a 32.4-point outing from mikelanta's Kenneth Walker. Meredith's Fan Club beat Long Live King Henry by 20.55 on the back of Puka Nacua (24.2) and a starting Patrick Mahomes (25.25), even though the far bigger number on that roster, C.J. Stroud's 32.55, never left the bench spot it was parked in.

The league's top individual scorer was Tetairoa McMillan, who put up 40.2 points for Screaming Eagles in a 20.05-point win over Waffle House. That same roster produced the week's worst bench decision anywhere in the league: Drake Maye scored 38.85 points without taking a snap on the Screaming Eagles' bench while Matthew Stafford started and returned 14.85, a 24-point gap. It's the rare lineup mistake large enough to make a 40-point week feel like it happened almost by accident.

Mistakes were everywhere this week, not just in Philadelphia-adjacent quarterback rooms. demon44 left Romeo Doubs' 22.8 points on the bench during its blowout loss, and Long Live King Henry started a scoreless Rashee Rice over Devaughn Vele's 15.4. Nobody in the league finished the week with a clean lineup card.
transaction_desk:
The week's one real swing was Meredith's Fan Club burning a premium waiver slot — third in the order — on Oronde Gadsden, a tight end who returned 6.3 points in his first week on the roster. That's a real cost for a modest return so far, and worth tracking given the premium priority spent.

Most other moves cost nothing by design. demon44 used its last-place priority slot to grab Bryce Young off waivers, which is about as close to a free swing as this league allows, and it paid off immediately — 30.75 points in his first week aboard. Silverbacks added Michael Penix as an uncontested free agent and got 17.95 points out of him right away, while also picking up Kendre Miller as a likely injury-insurance move behind Travis Etienne, which is a sensible depth add regardless of whether he ever sees the field. Joe Mama Angie Daddy's addition of Sione Vaki reads the same way, a depth pickup behind Jahmyr Gibbs rather than a speculative flier. Chuba Bucky Doo rounded out its bench with Darren Waller and Kalif Raymond, neither of which cost anything and neither of which has produced much yet (5.1 and 1.6 points respectively) — low cost, low reward moves that are fine as organizational depth but shouldn't be mistaken for difference-makers.

standings_narrative:
With four weeks down, the division winners currently set the top three seeds: Joe Mama Angie Daddy out of the Diamonds at 3-1, Chuba Bucky Doo out of the Hearts at 2-2, and Pukachu Chews You out of the Clubs at 2-2. The next two best records outside those divisions fill out seeds four and five — Dak to the Future at 3-1 and Long Live King Henry at 2-2, both left out of the top three only because they don't have the best record in their own division.

The sixth and final spot doesn't go by record at all — it goes to whichever remaining team has scored the most points on the season, and right now that's mikelanta, sitting at 1-3 but with 540.05 points, more than several teams with winning records. Screaming Eagles sit just below that points line as the current bubble team, with Silverbacks, Waffle House, Broke Dak Mountain, and Meredith's Fan Club all still mathematically alive but on the outside looking in.
look_ahead: Next week, Chuba Bucky Doo faces Silverbacks, and Joe Mama Angie Daddy gets Broke Dak Mountain in a matchup that looks lopsided on paper after the week each team just had. Waffle House draws Meredith's Fan Club, Long Live King Henry faces Screaming Eagles, Meredith's Fan Club's division rival Dak to the Future takes on demon44, and mikelanta gets a shot at Pukachu Chews You, a potential statement game for a team that keeps outscoring its record.

running_jokes: Bench mismanagement is now a confirmed two-week trend for every single team in the league — not a fluke, a pattern.
mikelanta keeps piling up points without piling up wins, now the likely points-based wildcard at 1-3.
Screaming Eagles got the league's highest individual scorer and the league's worst bench decision in the same week.
